Apple's annual September iPhone launch event is still roughly two months away. However, this year will be different — not all iPhone models will debut simultaneously, as only the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the brand-new foldable iPhone will be released in September. Here's an explanation of why.

The iPhone lineup is getting bigger

Over the past few years, the annual iPhone lineup has gradually expanded. Just a few years ago, there were only three new models each year: the iPhone 11, iPhone 11 Pro, and iPhone 11 Pro Max. In 2020, the iPhone 12 mini was added, bringing the yearly release count to four; in 2022, the iPhone 12 mini was replaced by the iPhone 14 Plus, which later gave way to the iPhone Air.

With the launch of the iPhone 16e, the annual release cycle grew to five models. Add the iPhone Ultra into the mix, and there will be six iPhones per year. Releasing them all at once would certainly make for a lively event, but it would also feel extremely crowded.

Therefore, Apple has decided to switch to a staggered release schedule.

Two iPhone launches: fall and spring

The iPhone 18 lineup will feature six models: iPhone 18, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2, and iPhone Ultra.

This staggered release arrangement has a clear theme: flagship models in the fall, mid- and low-end models in the spring. It looks like it will play out as follows:

  • Fall 2026: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Ultra
  • Spring 2027: iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2

When the iPhone lineup expanded to four models, the fourth model has historically had a lukewarm reception at launch, whether it was the iPhone mini or the iPhone Plus. So Apple believes it should be clearly separated — giving the additional phones their own dedicated spotlight.

However, with the iPhone 18, the situation is slightly different. Reports suggest Apple is exploring merging the production technology of the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, meaning the differences between the two devices could narrow significantly.

It's unclear whether this approach will result in major improvements for the iPhone 18e or a downgrade for the iPhone 18 — but the distinction between the two may come down to subtle differences in display panels and cameras.

Summary

In summary, assuming the iPhone Air doesn't end up being cancelled (which I certainly hope won't happen) — this is the new iPhone lineup going forward. Three models in the fall, three more in the spring. Hopefully, this arrangement will help Apple more clearly define the focus of each launch and reach the right audience.

Another possible outcome is that the average selling price of iPhones will rise, because users eager to get their hands on the new models will have no choice but to buy the iPhone 18 Pro rather than a more affordable option.

Whether a staggered product lineup will actually help each model sell better remains to be seen, but this is the initial plan so far.

What do you think of Apple's plan to stagger iPhone releases? Will you pick one up this fall, or wait until spring? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
